summary: Backend-only validation of task-schedule (appointment window) feature and by-service busy-exclusion + day-of-week (Mon=0) fix. 10/10 pytest tests passed against the deployed preview backend.
critical_code_review_comments: Notification response field is 'notification_type' (not 'type'). Frontend/clients relying on a 'type' key would silently miss task_scheduled notifications. Consider aliasing or documenting.

schedule_task validates duration<=0 and start_time containing ':' only. Malformed times like '9x:00' still pass through to _add_minutes which swallows the ValueError and returns the input unchanged; this could persist invalid confirmed_end_time. Suggest strict re.match('^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$') on start_time and reject fractional-only durations that are not 0.5 multiples.
_add_minutes clamps to 23:59 silently — a start=23:00, duration=3 would set end=23:59 without any error. Consider rejecting windows that overflow the day.

server.py is 12,776 lines. Strongly recommend splitting into feature modules (tasks, availability, executors, notifications, auth) — file size violates the >700-line guideline and hurts maintainability.
seed_data_creation: Ensured provider user_dc5e0dd73212 has an active Monday (day_of_week=0) availability slot 08:00-20:00. Repeatedly re-scheduled the existing task task_389d5fbe1766 to exercise reschedule + busy-window flows. No new users, bookings, or notifications collections were seeded outside these tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_task_schedule.py covers: 0.5h math (09:00+2.5h=>11:30, 09:00+1.5h=>10:30), reschedule flag flip, duration<=0 400, malformed time 400, client 403, unknown/foreign task 403/404, client notification 'task_scheduled' with 12h-formatted times, day-of-week filter (Mon=0 slot => provider returned only on Mondays), and busy exclusion (confirmed 09:00-11:00 window hides provider at time=10:00 but not at time=12:00). Provider seed has service_radius_km=30, lat=42.0294, lng=-87.8656 (Niles IL), skill 'Electrical work' in category 'repairs'. Existing task task_389d5fbe1766 is assigned to that provider.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature works as specified. Only note: the notification payload uses 'notification_type' rather than 'type'; the first pytest run failed because the assertion looked for 'type'. Fixed the assertion to accept both.
